classifiedFinding.title: _recomputeSchedule reads balanceOf(this) directly, allowing donation griefing to perturb runway and lock excess phUSD

classification.assetImpact: No theft. Donor pays for the perturbation; donated phUSD becomes irreversibly committed to staker rewards or, if all stakers exit, locked in the contract (no admin sweep — see L-15). Schedule predictability is impacted (windowEnd shifts unpredictably with donations).
attackPath: 1. Owner is about to call setTargetAPY to reduce APY.
2. Attacker front-runs with a phUSD transfer of size D to the staker contract.
3. _recomputeSchedule reads balance = pre + D, sets rewardBudget = pre + D + mintDebt - committedDebt, extends windowEnd by D / newRate.
4. The protocol now has a longer runway than the owner intended; stakers receive D of unexpected subsidy from the attacker.
classification.likelihood: low - attacker pays for the grief; no rational profit motive beyond niche schedule manipulation.
classification.assumptions: Attacker willing to spend D of their own phUSD to cause a one-way subsidy and runway perturbation.

classifiedFinding.justification: Low. State-handling / donation-perturbation issue with no asset theft. The donor subsidises the protocol; the resulting locked-funds and predictability surface are real but bounded by the attacker's willingness to spend. Combine with L-15 (no admin sweep) for the full lock-in concern. Recommendation: track an internal accountedBudget counter and use it instead of balanceOf(this) inside _recomputeSchedule.
